name: Drupal
description: An open source content management framework.
summary: Drupal allows AI-assisted contributions, but contributors must disclose significant AI-generated code or text and take full responsibility for it, including verifying it and ensuring GPL-compatible licensing. AI-generated issue text, comments and merge request descriptions must be reviewed and written in the contributor's own words rather than pasted verbatim.

evidence.quote: If you use an AI tool to generate a significant portion of the code or text you are submitting, you must disclose it. You must disclose this use regardless of how thoroughly you reviewed the output.
You must thoroughly verify all dependencies, logic, and security implications of AI-generated code before submitting.
You are solely responsible for ensuring that any AI-generated code you submit does not violate third-party copyrights and is fully compatible with the Drupal project's GPL license.
You are responsible for the words and code you post to an issue. AI tools often produce overly verbose output, making straightforward issues difficult to understand.

Using AI to generate issue summaries, comments, or reviews that lack independently verified technical insights (for example, using an AI tool to summarize a thread simply to gain contribution credits).

sources.title: Policy on the use of AI when contributing to Drupal | Issue procedures and etiquette | Drupal Wiki guide on Drupal.org
